h1. FCT Upload Endpoint — Frontend Contract

{info}
*Status:* Locked
*Audience:* Frontend integration
*Source:* {{fcvt-phase2-design.md}} §5; sample response {{UploadFCTResponse.json}}
*Owner:* Backend
{info}

h2. 1. Purpose

Phase 2 introduces {{POST /api/upload/fct}}, a new endpoint that accepts an {{.fct2}} archive (the FCT design tool's project export), parses {{Project.xml}} from inside the archive, and returns a {{ComAebMap}} JSON describing the project's AEB / IoExb / COM topology.

The {{ComAebMap}} is consumed by the validate-time preprocessor when the user subsequently calls {{/api/config/validate}}. The frontend's job is to:

* upload the archive when the user selects it
* hold the response shape in memory for the duration of the session
* surface upload-time failures to the user using the error codes defined below

This document is the contract the frontend wires against. It does not describe parser internals or the rules engine.

h2. 2. Request

*Method and path:* {{POST /api/upload/fct}}

*Body:* {{multipart/form-data}} with a single file part — the {{.fct2}} archive.

*Resource limits:*

* 10 MB file
* 15 MB request
* 20 MB threshold
* In-memory only — no disk spool
* Decompression ratio cap: 50:1
* Total uncompressed size cap: 50 MB

*File identification (server-side):*

* {{.fct2}} extension check
* ZIP magic-byte stream check on the first 8 KB – 40 KB of the upload

*Expected archive root layout:*

* 8 files at the root
* 0 to 2 trackplan folders (folders are optional; valid archives can have 0, 1, or 2)

Only {{Project.xml}} from within the archive is parsed. Trackplan XMLs are not opened.

h2. 3. Response — success (HTTP 200)

The response body is a {{ComAebMap}} JSON object. Full sample in {{UploadFCTResponse.json}}. The shape carries:

* *Project metadata* at the top level (project identifiers extracted from {{Project.xml}}).
* *AEB list* — each AEB with its {{Id}}, segment membership, and references to other AEBs.
* *acoIoExbs* — list of ACO-mode IoExbs. Each entry carries its host AEB and its resolved FMA. An ACO IoExb's resolved FMA may reference an AEB different from its host AEB — this is supported and not an error.
* *dtIoExbCount* — count of DT-mode IoExbs. Note: the inner DT data itself comes from the PDQ workbook, not from the FCT.
* *COM list* — COM entries with their forwarding and connection topology.

*ID serialisation:* all IDs are serialised as JSON *strings*, including numeric IDs. The frontend must treat them as opaque string identifiers.

h2. 4. Response — error contract

Only two external error codes. Both surface as the response body for a non-2xx HTTP status. The frontend renders the user-facing message; the code itself is the contract.

|| Code || Meaning ||
| {{FCT_TAMPERED}} | Cross-reference or invariant failure during {{ComAebMap}} build. XML parse failures also fold into this category. Catches the case where the FCT archive was manually edited after export. |
| {{FCT_INCOMPLETE_BASELINE}} | Pre-export incomplete-baseline FCT. Conditions that trigger this code: dangling {{CanConnections}}; chain with no COM; multi-COM chain without redundancy pairing; unsupported IoExb mode (including counting-head-output mode IoExbs, which are not in scope for Phase 2); duplicate or missing entity {{Id}} where {{Id}} is {{0}} or {{4096}}. |

*Pre-business-logic rejections* are returned as standard HTTP status codes and are _not_ folded into the two codes above:

* {{HTTP 400}} — malformed multipart (e.g. wrong content type, no file part, corrupted upload)
* {{HTTP 413}} — size exceedance (file, request, or threshold limit hit; uncompressed size cap exceeded; decompression ratio cap exceeded)

The frontend should distinguish HTTP-layer failures (400, 413) from business-logic failures (the two named codes) in its error UI, since the user remediation is different — fix-and-retry for the former, fix-the-source-FCT for the latter.

h2. 5. Sample response

The sample success response is attached as {{UploadFCTResponse.json}}. It is the source of truth for field names, nesting, and ID-as-string serialisation.

For any field present in the sample that this document does not explicitly call out, the sample is authoritative.

h2. 6. Out of scope for this contract

* Parser internals (how {{Project.xml}} is walked, how {{ComAebMap}} is constructed).
* The {{/api/upload/pdq}} endpoint (separate contract).
* The {{/api/config/validate}} endpoint and the Phase 2 response template (separate contract).
* The Agreed Output Phase 2 visual contract (separate workstream).

h2. 7. Acknowledgement

Frontend lead to confirm contract review in writing (Jira comment or Confluence page comment) before integration work begins.
